threads.body: The Javadoc here says "DO NOT USE OR OVERRIDE THIS METHOD", but the extractor API is designed so instrumentations can provide explicit values (and SqlClientAttributesExtractor even calls DbClientAttributesExtractor.onStartCommon() last specifically to allow explicit getter overrides). This wording is likely to confuse users and prevents legitimate cases where the operation name can’t be derived from raw SQL text (or raw SQL isn’t available). Consider rewording to describe the intended default behavior and when overriding is appropriate.

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/5795d344bb71a9296de17e4fd9b383d35ab177ac.

Reworded the getDbOperationName() Javadoc to steer SQL instrumentations toward raw query text and setSingleOperationAndCollection instead of overriding the SQL getter.

threads.body: Same as above: "DO NOT USE OR OVERRIDE" is overly absolute for a public getter. Even with SQL parsing enabled, there are valid cases where an instrumentation may need to provide a collection name explicitly. Rewording this to describe the default (parsed) behavior and the override semantics would make the API less confusing.

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/5795d344bb71a9296de17e4fd9b383d35ab177ac.

Reworded the getDbCollectionName() Javadoc the same way, including the semantic-convention caveat for databases that support query text with multiple collections in non-batch operations.

threads.body: In stable-only mode (emitStableDatabaseSemconv() true and emitOldDatabaseSemconv() false), SqlClientAttributesExtractor no longer consults SqlClientAttributesGetter#getDbQueryText() / #getDbQuerySummary(), even though their Javadoc says they can be used to explicitly provide those values. This makes the getters a no-op depending on configuration, and prevents instrumentations from supplying query text/summary when rawQueryTexts is empty/unavailable.

replies.body: No code change needed for this one. I updated the `SqlClientAttributesGetter` Javadocs instead so SQL instrumentations are directed not to override `getDbQueryText()` / `getDbQuerySummary()`, and to provide raw query text through `getRawQueryTexts()` so `SqlClientAttributesExtractor` can derive those attributes consistently.
